answer: Admission runs as a sealed auction for scarce identity slots. Each bid burns a non-refundable fee and locks a larger stake at one graph vertex, labeled with a unique juniper lot so the same collateral cannot be reused. Winning payouts then age in a slow settlement river whose flow is capped per controlling key. A sybil attacker must burn and lock fresh capital for every extra vertex, and splitting into many thin identities does not speed the river.
